entries.clue: By orchard, eat rotten type of food (12)

indicatorNotes.rotten: rotten fruit has gone bad, so the letters are spoiled into a new order

annotation.surface: A warning not to eat the windfalls rotting under the orchard trees.
annotation.walkthrough: The orchard and the rotten fruit make you think of apples, but all three words before 'rotten' are raw material.
annotation.definitionFit: Carbohydrate is a broad class of food, such as bread, pasta and potatoes.

entries.clue: Dog left length of hair (4)

blocks.note: a cur is a mongrel dog

annotation.surface: A dog has shed a clump of its fur.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Left' reads as a verb, the dog leaving hair behind, but it is only the abbreviation L.
annotation.definitionFit: A curl is a single coiled lock, a length of hair.

entries.clue: Annoyed in game, female ran off (7)

annotation.surface: A player got annoyed during a match and a woman stormed away.
annotation.walkthrough: RU for rugby union is a stock crossword game; 'in' only joins the definition to the wordplay.
annotation.definitionFit: Ruffled means put out or irritated, as in ruffled feathers.

entries.clue: Appearing to knock when kept ready (2,3)

blocks.note: an actor who is on is appearing on stage

annotation.surface: Someone shows up to knock at the door once everything is prepared.
annotation.walkthrough: ON for 'appearing' comes from the theatre: the actor is on.
annotation.definitionFit: Beer on tap is drawn straight from the barrel, so anything on tap is ready whenever wanted.

entries.clue: Agreeable chaps are second in country (3-3)

indicatorNotes.in: the S is put in the country's name

blocks.note: Yemen, in Arabia; it wraps round the S

annotation.surface: The friendliest men are found in second place in some nation's ranking.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Agreeable' is doing double duty in spirit: yes-men are not pleasant, they simply agree with everything.
annotation.definitionFit: Yes-men are people who always agree with their boss, so literally agreeable chaps.

entries.clue: About a hundred dash for lounge (7)

blocks.note: a dash is a short line

annotation.surface: Roughly a hundred people rush towards the lounge bar.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Lounge' looks like a room to dash into, but it is the verb: to lie back.
annotation.definitionFit: To recline is to lean back at ease, which is to lounge.

entries.clue: Little time to get skilled board (5)

indicatorNotes.Little: a little version of 'time' is its abbreviation, T

annotation.surface: With not much time, someone must become competent at a board game.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Board' suggests a board game or a committee, but here it is the old sense of a table for meals, as in bed and board.
annotation.definitionFit: A board is a flat surface for meals or work, which is a table.

entries.clue: Road to a building hidden away (7)

blocks.note: a shed is a simple building

annotation.surface: A path leads to a building tucked out of sight.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface pictures a secluded building; in fact 'hidden away' is the definition, a past participle like the answer.
annotation.definitionFit: Stashed means put somewhere secret, that is hidden away.

entries.clue: Starting to fall in line, backing overhaul (5)

indicatorNotes.Starting: the start of 'fall' is its first letter
indicatorNotes.in: that letter goes in the line

blocks.note: a tier is a row or line; it wraps round the F
reversal indicator: the whole five-letter string is read right to left

annotation.surface: Queue-jumpers start to fall into line, supporting a shake-up.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Backing' sounds like support for the overhaul; it is an order to read the letters backwards.
annotation.definitionFit: A refit is a thorough overhaul, especially of a ship.

entries.clue: Buck sat playing old instrument (7)

indicatorNotes.playing: the letters play about, rearranging themselves

annotation.surface: A young man sat down to play an antique instrument.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Playing' fits the musical surface perfectly, which hides its job as the rearranging signal.
annotation.definitionFit: The sackbut is the Renaissance ancestor of the trombone.

entries.clue: Evasive quality of a mule? (12)

blocks.note: the plain reading: the trait of dodging capture or questions
the surface wants the stubborn animal; the setter means a mule as backless indoor footwear, and the question mark flags the pun

annotation.surface: A stubborn mule refusing to be caught.
annotation.walkthrough: The animal is a red herring: a mule is also a backless slipper, so the quality of a mule is to be slipper-y.
annotation.definitionFit: Slipperiness is the quality of being evasive and hard to pin down.

entries.clue: Designate river during a drink (7)

indicatorNotes.during: the river flows during, that is inside, the drink

blocks.note: a pint; it wraps round the river

annotation.surface: Choosing someone while having a drink by the river.
annotation.walkthrough: The Po is the stock crossword river, as is the Dee.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: naming someone officially to a post is both.

entries.clue: Salesperson - one in the saddle, we hear (6)

indicatorNotes.we hear: what we hear is the sound, not the spelling

blocks.note: a pedaller sits in a bicycle saddle

annotation.surface: A travelling salesman on horseback, so people say.
annotation.walkthrough: The saddle suggests a horseman, but it belongs to a bicycle: the rider is a pedaller.
annotation.definitionFit: A pedlar is an itinerant seller of small goods.

entries.clue: Boy put hydrogen in cold liquor (7)

indicatorNotes.in: namely inside the word for cold

blocks.note: cool = cold; it wraps round the H
H is the chemical symbol for hydrogen
the instruction to place the H
container indicator: the H goes between the two O's of COOL

annotation.surface: A lad in a lab adds hydrogen to chilled spirits.
annotation.walkthrough: The chemistry fits a real fact: ethanol does contain hydrogen, which helps hide the symbol H.
annotation.definitionFit: Liquor is alcoholic drink, alcohol for short.

entries.clue: Heavens! There's a weapon in the river (4,2)

indicatorNotes.in the: the weapon is placed in the river's name

blocks.note: the Dee, a British river; it wraps round the weapon
an arm is a weapon, as in firearm
container indicator: the weapon splits the river after its second letter

annotation.surface: An exclamation of alarm on spotting a gun in the water.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Heavens!' works as the exclamation of the surface and as the definition itself.
annotation.definitionFit: Dear me! and Heavens! are both mild exclamations of surprise or dismay.

entries.clue: Ruled broadcast was wet (7)

indicatorNotes.broadcast: a broadcast is heard, so we get a sound

blocks.note: it rained = the weather was wet

annotation.surface: A weather forecaster announcing it had been a wet day.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Ruled' could be ruled lines or a verdict; the monarch's sense is the one needed.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a monarch holding the throne both governs and presides over the realm.

entries.clue: In Lisbon, said to be little growth (6)

indicatorNotes.In: the answer sits in the next words

annotation.surface: A report that something in Lisbon is supposedly small.
annotation.walkthrough: The comma between Lisbon and said does not stop the hidden run.
annotation.definitionFit: A bonsai is a deliberately dwarfed tree, a little growth.

entries.clue: Too chilled – so arranged for special neckwear? (3,6,3)

indicatorNotes.arranged: the letters are arranged in a new order

annotation.surface: Too cold outside, so someone sorts out a scarf.
annotation.walkthrough: An old school tie is worn by former pupils of a British private school, and stands for the network of privilege they share.
annotation.definitionFit: An old school tie is a tie in a school's colours, special because only former pupils may wear it; the question mark admits the loose phrasing.

entries.clue: Get rid of channel (5)

blocks.note: first sense: a verb, to discard or abandon
second sense: a noun, a trench dug to carry water

annotation.surface: An instruction to switch off a TV channel.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Channel' suggests television, but it is the dug trench.
annotation.definitionFit: Ditch as a verb means discard, and as a noun a drainage channel.

entries.clue: Notedly slow in regular government (5)

indicatorNotes.in: the answer is in the following words

annotation.surface: A complaint that normal government moves remarkably slowly.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Notedly' reads as 'notably', but means in musical notation: largo is a tempo marking.
annotation.definitionFit: Largo is the musical direction for a slow, broad tempo.

entries.clue: Colourful worker coming from Ryde (4)

indicatorNotes.coming from: the answer comes out of the letters of the town

blocks.note: anagram fodder; Ryde is a town on the Isle of Wight

annotation.surface: A flamboyant labourer who hails from a seaside town.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Colourful' suggests a lively character, but a dyer literally works with colour.
annotation.definitionFit: A dyer colours cloth for a living.

entries.clue: Cuts on chest treated (7)

indicatorNotes.treated: the letters are processed into a new form

annotation.surface: A nurse has dressed wounds on a patient's chest.
annotation.walkthrough: The medical picture makes 'treated' look like first aid; it only reshuffles ON CHEST.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: small V-shaped nicks in an edge, like those on a tally stick.

entries.clue: Gangling youth leader telephoned before (5)

indicatorNotes.leader: the leader of 'youth' is its first letter
indicatorNotes.before: the phone call comes before that letter

annotation.surface: A lanky youth club leader had phoned earlier.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Youth leader' looks like a job title; it just means the first letter of 'youth'.
annotation.definitionFit: Rangy describes someone tall and long-limbed, which is gangling.

entries.clue: Tablet, one back in soup, is hot stuff (6,6)

indicatorNotes.back: the tablet and one are turned back to front
indicatorNotes.in: that result goes inside the soup

blocks.note: chowder is a thick soup; it wraps round the reversed piece
container indicator: the reversed piece goes after the soup's first two letters

annotation.surface: A medicine dropped into soup turns out to be fiery.
annotation.walkthrough: The comma after 'Tablet' tempts you to read it as the definition; 'hot stuff' at the end is the real one, with 'is' as the link. Chowder is a thick, creamy soup, often of clams.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by description: the ground dried peppers are spicy-hot, taken literally rather than as slang for something desirable.
